invariants: Weapon-side proprietary/dovetail slots use a leaf compatibility type, never a broad organizational parent.
Organizational parents are never serialized directly into final weapon slots or final optic modules.
A final optic prefab has one mount-family AttachmentType; multi-mount optics use thin child wrapper prefabs per family.
RIS1913 uses the Bohemia length hierarchy; use the narrowest suitable rail class.
Adapters bridge mount families explicitly instead of widening the native weapon slot.
Every final optic must have at least one compatible slot and every optic slot must have at least one approved optic.
Compatibility is checked statically by transitive type inheritance and an explicit allowlist.
Sight mechanics remain separate from attachment compatibility.

weapon_slot_issues: armst_SVD uses AttachmentOpticsDovetailAK rather than an SVD-specific type.
VSS, VAL, 9A91, VSK94, AKM and SVD share AttachmentOpticsDovetailAK, allowing AK-typed optics across distinct families.
Groza uses AttachmentOpticsRIS1913; verify that the physical rail should accept the full RIS hierarchy or choose a narrower rail-length class.
G36 already uses the strict custom AttachmentOpticsG36 pattern.

migration_order: Add new ARMST optic compatibility marker classes without deleting existing types.
Create thin optic wrapper prefabs per mount family from shared optic-body bases.
Migrate AK, SVD, VSS/VAL and 9A91/VSK94 slots one family at a time.
Generate the compatibility matrix and fail CI for orphan optics, broad proprietary slots and unapproved cross-family pairs.
Retire obsolete broad mappings only after Workbench validation.
